newsitem.title: USA: Compaq to buy Tandem in $3 billion stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Compaq to buy Tandem in $3 billion stock swap.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., the world's leading supplier of personal computers, said on Monday it had agreed to acquire Tandem Computers Inc. in a stock swap worth about $3 billion.
Compaq had been reported in merger talks with several companies, including Digital Equipment Corp., Gateway 2000 Inc. and Micron Electronics Inc.
Tandem will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Compaq.
The tax-free deal will be accretive to earnings immediately, Compaq said.
Compaq will issue some 29 million shares in exchange for all of the stock of Tandem. The exchange ratio will be about 0.21 Compaq share for each share of Tandem.
Because the merger transaction will be a pooling of interests, Compaq's board of directors has rescinded its previously announced systematic share repurchase program.
The merger is subject to approval by Tandem shareholders, clearance under anti-trust law, and other customary closing conditions.
The deal is expected to be completed in the third quarter.

Compaq Chief Executive Officer Eckhard Pfeiffer said of the proposed merger, "Our total addressable market has been doubled to approximately $650 billion. This offers opportunity for significant revenue growth.

"We will truly offer complete solutions, from handhelds and portables, to networked desktops and workstations, all the way to Windows NT servers and the Himalaya range of massively parallel commercial systems."
Tandem Chairman Tom Perkins has been invited to join the Compaq board of directors.
Houston-based Compaq is the fifth largest computer company in the world. In 1996 it reported worldwide sales of $18.1 billion.
Tandem, a $1.9 billion company headquartered in Cupertino, Calif., was founded in 1974 and employs nearly 7,000 people worldwide.
